The Rust client owns URL resolution, link lifecycle, request framing, Git list/fetch/push queues, repository management, releases, permissions, and work-item operations through a transport-neutral request seam.
Client operations are exercised against the deterministic local node transport; live Reticulum wiring remains an integration adapter over the same request paths.
The server-side client wrapper shares the validated request transport and implements repository, release, permission, and work-item request operations.
The node loads bare repositories, enforces hierarchical permissions, dispatches all registered Git/release/work/permission paths, and records activity.
All pinned server handlers and lifecycle/statistics methods are covered by the transport-neutral service and isolated Git/work/release fixtures.
